correctness.rationale: The terminality proof agrees with the general two-heavy Reid--Tai classification. Fletcher's subset criterion reduces to the singleton heavy variable \(a\): the possible degree conditions are exactly \(a\mid D\), \(a\mid D-1\), or \(a\mid D-b\), which reduce to the stated three divisibilities; the other heavy singleton and pair conditions are automatic. Inclusion--exclusion gives the exact count using \(\gcd(r,2r-2)=\gcd(r,2)\) and coprimality with \(2r-1\). Standard divisor-summatory identities give the stated main term and linear coefficient. Independent exact finite checks of the divisor criterion and count agreed with the package; the infinite assertion is supported by the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: A stronger published SCOPE theorem already gives an iff quasismoothness criterion for every two-heavy \(\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\): with \(d=b-a\), the \(a\)-condition is divisibility by one of \(r,r+d,r+d-1\), and the \(b\)-condition by one of \(r,r-d,r-d-1\). Substituting the audited first terminal layer \(d=r-1\), \(b=a+r-1\), makes the \(b\)-condition automatic because \(b\mid0\) and gives exactly \(a\mid r\), \(a\mid2r-1\), or \(a\mid2r-2\). The published triangular theorem also supplies terminality for exactly \(1\le a\le2r-2\). The remaining count and summatory asymptotic are routine inclusion--exclusion and standard divisor-summatory identities. Thus the whole final claim is prior-implied under the required implication standard.
